entries.title: Persuasion Listening: Worse Than Strangers
entries.hook: Why does Anne think they are worse than strangers? Listen for the contrast.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Once, Anne and Captain Wentworth had been everything to each other. Now they spoke only with the politeness required between strangers.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: But real strangers can still become acquainted. Anne believes that their shared past makes even a new beginning impossible. That is why the distance feels worse.

entries.prompt: Why are they worse than strangers?
entries.answer: Their shared past prevents a simple new beginning.
entries.visualBrief: Elegant Regency drawing room, Anne and Captain Wentworth stand far apart with a social gathering between them, restrained emotional distance, hands fully out of frame, no readable text.

entries.title: Restaurant English: Catch the Final Dressing
entries.hook: The first choice is unavailable. Can you catch the final dressing?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Sorry, we have no Caesar dressing this evening. We have lemon dressing or no dressing.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: The first choice was Caesar, but the final choice was lemon. When you hear unavailable, remove the old answer and listen for the replacement.

entries.prompt: Which dressing is in the final order?
entries.visualBrief: Bright modern restaurant listening scene, two adult hosts shown chest-up with simple salad icons between them, hands fully below frame, teal and orange, no readable text.

entries.title: Restaurant English: Let Me Check That
entries.hook: One phrase can stop a wrong restaurant order before the kitchen starts.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: Let me check that: one chicken wrap with extra cheese and no chips.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Good. Repeat only the final version, not every change in the conversation.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: And one small Greek salad with lemon dressing.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Exactly. Let me check that tells the listener you are confirming the important details.

entries.visualBrief: Warm anime restaurant counter, adult woman and adult man shown from shoulders up confirming a takeaway order, hands out of frame, clean teal and amber composition, no readable text.

entries.title: Persuasion Listening: Cold Politeness
entries.hook: Polite language can still feel painfully cold when two people share a past.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Captain Wentworth sees Anne near the instrument and immediately offers her the seat.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: His words are perfectly courteous: I beg your pardon, madam, this is your seat.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Yet the formal distance hurts Anne more than open anger. The tone shows that politeness and warmth are not the same thing.

entries.prompt: Why does the polite sentence hurt?
entries.answer: Its formal distance replaces their former closeness.
entries.visualBrief: Regency music room, Anne near a piano and Captain Wentworth standing at a respectful distance, restrained sadness, hands obscured by furniture, no readable text.
